senses.gloss: to overshadow, to obscure, to put to shame; to censure.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 92b:10">Snh. 92ᵇ</cite> <he>היו מְגַנִּין את החמה וכ׳</he> obscured the sun with their beauty.

<cite ref="Gittin 58a:4">Gitt. 58ᵃ</cite> <he>היו מג׳ את הפז וכ׳</he> they outshone the finest gold with their beauty. Snh. l. c. <he>ביקש לְגַנּוֹת וכ׳</he> he would have attempted to excel all the praises &c.—
Sabb. 33ᵇ שגי׳ who criticised (the Roman government); a. fr.—Part. pass. מְגוּנֶּה deserving to be covered up, reprehensible, indecent; ugly.
<cite ref="Pesachim 3a:10">Pes. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר מג׳</he> an ugly expression e.g. <cite ref="I00529"><he>טמא</he></cite> in place of <he>לא טהור</he>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 33b:28">Ber. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>הרי זה מג׳</he> he is to be reprehended; <cite ref="Berakhot 45b">ib. 45ᵇ</cite>, opp. <he>משובח</he>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to make one’s self reprehensible, to become repulsive.
units: <cite ref="Chagigah 15b:5">Ḥag. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>ומה למִתְגַּנִּין בה וכ׳</he> if such regard is paid to those who abuse the knowledge of the Law &c., opp. <he>משתבחין</he>.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 41a">Kidd. 41ᵃ</cite> he may see in her <he>דבר מגינה ותִתְגַּנֶּה עליו</he> something objectionable, and she may become repulsive to him.
